# Name authority control

A name authority record fixes one preferred form of a name and lists every
variant form that should lead a searcher to it. Catalogue records point at the
authority by its control number, never by the name string, so correcting a
preferred form corrects every record that uses it at once.

A new authority is created only when the name cannot be matched to an existing
one with confidence. Two people with the same name are distinguished by adding
dates, and where no dates are available, by a fuller form of the name.

A preferred form is changed only by the cataloguing lead. The old form is
retained as a variant rather than deleted, because a searcher who learned the
old form must still land on the right record.

Corporate bodies follow the same rules as persons, with one difference: a
subordinate body is entered under its parent where the subordinate name cannot
stand alone as a meaningful heading.
